New analysis: between country explanation for rates

We know that changes over time in both a) how retractions are reported, and b) retraction watch’s data processing practice for them make temporal patterns complex to interpret. What is more robust is inter-country comparisons.

Applying reasons: United Kingdom vs Other OECD

Statistical comparison of the retraction reasons between the UK and the rest of the OECD excluding the mass retractions. The for each period (pre and post 2017) and retraction reason, computes the proportion and count of retractions in the UK and the rest of the OECD, the difference in proportions, a two-sample proportion test p-value and its Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment.

Removing the reasons that appear less than 30 times among the whole OECD.

Training a logistic regression to predict United Kingdom vs Other OECD countries based on the retraction reasons of each paper.

Showing the ROC curve.

Analysis of results.

Logistic regression predicting United Kingdom (878 papers) vs Other OECD (8285 papers) from 77 reasons.

McFadden pseudo R-squared: 0.046 (0 = no better than the overall proportion of United Kingdom).

5 reasons are significant (adjusted p < 0.05); 0 coefficients are unreliable and ignored.

Reasons that most increase the odds of United Kingdom: withdrawn as out of date (odds of United Kingdom x8.95); retract and replace (odds of United Kingdom x1.96); concerns issues about article (odds of United Kingdom x1.95).

Reasons that most increase the odds of Other OECD: concerns issues about human subject welfare (odds of United Kingdom x0.18); duplication of in image (odds of United Kingdom x0.62).
